title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview

This document is the canonical Company Handbook page for employees and candidates. It summarizes: what it’s like to work at Redwood, our role tiers and career ladders, benefits and perks, high-level hiring and onboarding process, and the primary internal tools new hires will use. It is intended for all employees, hiring managers, and people-ops partners.

1) Working at Redwood — culture and expectations

Short intro
- Redwood is an engineering-first, product-minded company focused on shipping reliable inference products. We prioritize psychological safety, ownership, and operational rigor.
- We expect every engineer and product contributor to: ship iteratively, document decisions, and treat production as the primary interface to customers.

Core behaviors
- Own outcomes: be accountable for product quality and reliability.
- Communicate early: use Slack, RFCs, and Confluence for asynchronous coordination.
- Prioritize users: measure impact with customer-facing metrics and post-deploy checks.

Working norms
- Office / remote: hybrid model; core collaboration days are Tuesday/Wednesday. Team-specific arrangements are set by managers.
- Async-first communication: use Confluence for design docs and RFCs; prefer structured PR descriptions.
- Meeting guidelines: invitees only, agendas required, 25/50/75 minute blocks.

2) Roles & career ladders (engineering, product, design, SRE)

Summary
- We maintain discipline-specific ladders with competency markers for IC and manager paths. Ladders are skills- and impact-based rather than purely tenure-based.

Ladder highlights (short table)
| Function | Typical Levels | Focus areas |
|--------|---------------|------------|
| Engineering | IC2, IC3, Senior, Staff, Principal | System design, runtime performance, ownership |
| Product | Associate PM, PM, Senior PM, Staff PM | Product outcomes, customer research, roadmap |
| Design | Product Designer, Senior Designer, Lead | UX, research, design systems |
| SRE/Infra | SRE, Senior SRE, Staff SRE | SLOs, incident response, capacity planning |

Promotion criteria (common expectations)
- Clear impact on customers or engineering productivity.
- Demonstrated technical breadth and deep ownership for IC tracks.
- Leadership and mentorship for senior levels.
- Successful delivery of cross-team initiatives for staff/principal.

How to prepare a promotion packet
1. Gather artifacts: PRs, on-call incident ownership, metrics demonstrating impact.
2. Write a one-page summary aligned to the ladder competencies.
3. Share draft with your manager and 2 reviewers.
4. Submit to people-ops using the promotion template in Confluence; expect review cycle (3–6 weeks).

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

Core benefits
- Health: medical, dental, vision (US-based); equivalent local offerings for EMEA/APAC.
- Paid time off: 20 days PTO + company holidays and 10 company-wide flexible days per year.
- Parental leave: 16 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary (top-up to local statutory where applicable).
- Retirement: 401(k) matching (US) and country-appropriate equivalents.

Perks & allowances
- Learning & development stipend: $1,500 USD / year.
- Home office stipend: one-time $800 USD for equipment; ongoing monthly internet stipend.
- Conference policy: up to two conferences per employee per year (manager approval).
- Commuter / wellness reimbursements where applicable.

Expense & benefits administration
- Submit claims via the Benefits portal (Rippling for payroll/benefits admin).
- People-ops owns benefits enrollment windows; reach out to people-ops@redwood.com for exceptions.

4) Hiring & onboarding overview

Hiring principles
- Hire for impact, craft, and teammates who help us scale. We use a structured interview loop with calibrated rubrics to reduce bias.
- Role profiles and scorecards are required for every open role before a req is posted.

Recruiting stages (high level)
1. Requisition approval: hiring manager + hiring committee sign-off.
2. Sourcing & screen: recruiter screens, hiring manager phone screen.
3. Interview loop: 4–5 interviews (role-specific exercise, system design/technical, cross-functional partner).
4. Debrief & hire decision: calibrated rubric and compensation approval.
5. Offer & negotiation: recruiter owns offer extension; people-ops signs off on compensation bands.

Onboarding checklist (first 90 days)
- Day 0: welcome email, IT provisioning request.
- Day 1: orientation session (company values, benefits overview, security training).
- Week 1: meet the team, set 30/60/90 goals with manager, onboarding checklist complete for required access.
- Month 1: deliver first small project or ramp task; join product and engineering rituals.
- Month 3: formal 90-day check-in with manager and people-ops.

New hire manager responsibilities
- Curate the first 90-day growth plan.
- Assign a buddy and an onboarding project tied to a measurable outcome.
- Conduct weekly 1:1s for first 3 months and enable cross-team introductions.

5) Internal tools & access (core systems new hires will use)

Primary tools and purpose
- Slack: real-time communication. Join channels listed in the team onboarding page.
- Confluence: documentation hub (this source). Use templates for RFCs, PRDs, and runbooks.
- GitHub: code hosting and PR reviews. Repos are grouped by product area.
- Jira: engineering task tracking; follow team workflows for issue types and reviews.
- Rippling: HR and payroll (benefits enrollment).
- Okta: single sign-on. Use Okta to onboard cloud accounts (GCP/AWS).
- PagerDuty: on-call and incident alerts for SRE and service owners.

Access request flow
1. Complete the IT provisioning form (link: https://internal.redwood.com/it-provisioning).
2. Manager approves and assigns required repo/team access.
3. Okta SSO provisioned automatically; if not, contact infra-ops@redwood.com.
4. Confirm access within 48 hours; if blocked, open a ticket with IT support.

Security & compliance notes
- MFA is required for all accounts.
- Use company-managed keys for any access to production systems; never store secrets in plaintext.
- Follow the Data Classification table (see related security-and-compliance docs) before sharing customer data.

6) Career development, learning, and mentorship

Programs
- Mentorship program: opt-in, matched by people-ops each quarter.
- Manager enablement: training for managers on feedback and performance reviews.
- Internal mobility: roles posted internally for 10 business days before external posting.

Learning paths
- Technical growth: internal workshops on model-serving, performance optimization, and profiling.
- Leadership: career ladder workshops and promotion calibration sessions.

7) Common procedures and FAQs

How do I request flexible work?
- Talk to your manager; submit a flexible work agreement to people-ops for approval.

How do I escalate an interpersonal issue?
- First speak with your manager or assigned buddy. If unresolved, open a confidential case with people-ops at people-ops@redwood.com.

Where are the templates for design docs or RFCs?
- Confluence > Templates > RFCs and PRDs, and in the eng-developer-experience > docs-site area.

8) Appendix: quick reference tables

Promotion packet required artifacts (table)
| Artifact | Required? | Notes |
|---------|-----------|-------|
| Impact summary | Yes | One-page, aligned to ladder competencies |
| PR & review links | Yes | Highlight ownership and technical contributions |
| 2+ peer reviews | Preferred | Include cross-team reviewers |
| Manager recommendation | Yes | Include suggested level and rationale |

IT provisioning required access (table)
| Role | Minimum access set |
|------|------------------|
| Engineering IC | GitHub repos, Jira write, Confluence edit, Slack, dev GCP/AWS sandbox |
| SRE | Above + PagerDuty, production read, monitoring dashboards |
| Product | Confluence, Jira, analytics dashboards, limited GitHub access |

Contact list
- people-ops@redwood.com — benefits, payroll, onboarding exceptions
- infra-ops@redwood.com — provisioning, Okta, cloud accounts
- security@redwood.com — incident reporting, data classification questions

Document maintenance
- Owner: people-ops.
- Review cadence: annual (every Jan) or ad-hoc when policies change.
- Last reviewed by: Marcus Lee, Sofia Ramirez (2026-02-15).

End of document. For any missing details or exceptions, please contact people-ops@redwood.com.
